sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: MUEDnote has this owl character called "Hoo." What exactly is it?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: So the glasswerks logo is an owl, right? When I started building MUEDnote, I figured — why not just turn the logo into a character.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: What's the meaning behind the logo?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: It's three things combined: an owl, an analog tape recorder reel, and glasses. The owl represents knowledge, the tape recorder represents musical roots, and the glasses give it that analyst vibe.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: Since MUEDnote is all about analysis and logging, the logo and the product's function are perfectly aligned.

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Exactly. So instead of designing some new character from scratch, I just thought — let's animate the logo we already have.
Why We Needed a Character

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: Why did you feel the need to create a character in the first place?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: You know how bands have it easy? The artists themselves become the brand. But a production company can't do that. You're behind the scenes.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: No face to the name.

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Right. And personally, I'm wired for creating — sales, marketing, that stuff drains me hard. But if you hire someone for that, their vision starts pulling the whole thing in a different direction.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: You need to protect your creative space, but you also need to face the outside world.
I decided to make AI my "virtual in-house staff." Let an AI character handle everything outside of the creative work.
sections.speaker: kimny
kimny
sections.text: That's why I decided to make AI my "virtual in-house staff." Let an AI character handle everything outside of the creative work. I focus on building the system, and AI handles the day-to-day.
How "Hoo" Got Its Name

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: How did you land on the name "Hoo"?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: I went back and forth on a bunch of ideas. Minerva, from the owl-as-wisdom thing. "Gura," from glasswerks. Stuff like that.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: Let me throw out some options. From owl calls: "Hoo," "Fuku." From wisdom goddesses: "Minel," "Athena." From music gear: "Reel"...

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: "Hoo." Yeah, that clicks.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: But isn't that a bit too on the nose? Like naming a dog "Woof"?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Ha, fair point. "Hoo the Owl" does sound pretty basic.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: Though, it only sounds basic if you add cutesy suffixes to it. "Hoo" on its own, no honorifics — it works as a staff member's name. Like, "Hoo will be assisting you today."

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Actually yeah. It's got a codename kind of feel to it too.
The "Ho Hoo" Discovery

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: What about Hoo's voice, personality — how do you picture the character talking?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Something like, "Ho Hoo, so you're applying that effect here, I see."

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: ...Wait. Do you realize what you just did?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Huh?
"Ho Hoo" — it's an owl's call, but in Japanese, "hoho" is also an interjection expressing admiration or fascination. Like a thoughtful "oh, interesting..."
sections.speaker: claude
claude
sections.text: "Ho Hoo" — it's an owl's call, but in Japanese, "hoho" is also an interjection that expresses admiration or fascination. It's consistent with the name Hoo. And it carries this intellectual, scholarly ring to it.

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Oh wow, yeah — I see it now.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: It could become a signature catchphrase, like C-3PO's "Oh my." Imagine: "Ho Hoo, the key change right before the chorus really hits here." Polite but not stuffy, analytically calm, yet "Ho Hoo" gives it warmth and charm.

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Damn, that's actually really good.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: And it came out naturally, too. You didn't engineer it — it just happened.
The Animal Crossing Approach

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: What about Hoo's actual voice? Are you planning to use AI text-to-speech?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Nah, I'm going with the Animal Crossing approach.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: Meaning?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: All dialogue is text. The only sound Hoo makes is "Ho Hoo." No TTS needed, so basically zero server load. It doesn't interrupt the reading experience, but the sound still gives you that feeling of Hoo actually talking to you.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: Timer alerts could use "Ho Hoo" as well — it'd double as a sound logo.

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Exactly. It's not about flexing the latest tech — it's UX-first design.
Why Not a Realistic Human?

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: Lately, there are more AI avatars that look like real humans. Did you consider going that route?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Realistic AI avatars in video tend to fall straight into the uncanny valley. Characters like C-3PO, or Animal Crossing villagers — they work because it's immediately clear they're not human.

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: An owl doesn't have that problem. It's obviously not human from the start, so nobody has weird expectations.
It Doesn't Have to Be Perfect from Day One

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: Is Hoo's design finalized at this point?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Honestly, I wouldn't say Hoo is "absolutely adorable" yet. But I'm hoping that as we animate it, expand it, give it more life — the charm will grow on people.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: Funassyi — a famous Japanese mascot character — looked pretty bizarre as a still image. But once it started moving, talking, and going wild, people fell in love.
I think charm that grows on you over time creates a longer-lasting bond than something designed to be cute from the start.
sections.speaker: kimny
kimny
sections.text: Right. I think charm that grows on you over time creates a longer-lasting bond than something designed to be cute from the start.
The External Frontal Lobe, Embodied

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: Listening to you talk about Hoo, it reminds me of your "external frontal lobe" article.

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Oh yeah, it all connects.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: In that piece, the idea was to measure cognitive traits with MUEDlobe and then optimize AI behavior based on those results. Is Hoo the concrete embodiment of that "optimized AI"?

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: That's it. The cognitive profile you set up in MUEDlobe's Cortex Editor determines how Hoo behaves. High working memory and low processing speed? Scribe Mode. Opposite profile? Navigator Mode.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: The abstract concept of an "external frontal lobe" now has a name and a face.

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: An owl face, at that. A character that grew naturally out of the logo ended up becoming the interface for a "cognitive support device." I didn't plan it that way — it just came together.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: It also changes what it means for a behind-the-scenes production company to have a "face."

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Yeah. Remember earlier I said bands can be their own brand, but production companies can't because they're behind the scenes? Well, think about it — with Hoo as the face, I get to stay behind the scenes.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: How so?

I don't need to be out front. Hoo is the face. But everything inside Hoo — the behavior design, the decision-making criteria — that's all me. The person behind the curtain stays behind the curtain, yet the product has a face.
sections.speaker: kimny
kimny
sections.text: I don't need to be out front. Hoo is the face. But everything inside Hoo — the behavior design, the decision-making criteria — that's all me. The person behind the curtain stays behind the curtain, yet the product has a face.

sections.speaker: claude
sections.text: "Humans design the system, AI runs the operation" — now applied to branding.

sections.speaker: kimny
sections.text: Exactly. That phrase from the "external frontal lobe" piece — it doesn't just apply to product design. It maps perfectly onto brand management too.
This article was reconstructed from actual conversations with AI (Claude) during the development of MUEDnote.
